judgment.notes: The symmetric Fourier truncations are smooth, real, mean-zero and remain in the same H^gamma ball. Since gamma>0, their L2 norms and that of u0 are at most R, so N001's stability applies with B0=2R. N005 applies to the inverse derivatives and H^1 products in S002; zero-mode removal handles intermediate products with nonzero mean. N011 applies to each truncation with exactly the same T,gamma,R,C,tau0.

S001 obtains uniform-in-time exact L2 convergence. In S002 every F_tau and H_tau term is continuous into L2 by the stated H^1 algebra estimate, bounded Fourier multipliers and the continuous scalar mean of f^2; tau^{-1} is harmless for fixed tau>0. These maps preserve reality and zero mean, so their finite iterates are defined and continuous. S003 passes the uniform smooth-data estimate through convergence at the finitely many grid points. Neither an infinite-step limit nor a numerical H^gamma bound is used.

All substantive inputs are direct: H001-H003 supply the ranges, N001 supplies exact solutions and stability, N005 supplies operator/product estimates, and N011 supplies the uniform smooth-data error. F001 and F002 precede their use in S003. The norm-ball assumption L1 is retained in F001 and discharged into P. The arbitrary datum and admissible positive integer L are quantified; C,tau0 come from N011 independently of either. The background notes only justify routine local steps along the given route.

scope: Coverage is reviewer-reported; reading alone is not mathematical assessment.
